title: Limitation (DRAFT)
description: A named gap: something this profile cannot do, or something this document/run could not do. Limitations live in the artifact, not in a doc comment — a limitation a reviewer can read and a consumer cannot is not a declaration.

code.$comment: Stable kebab-case, matched by callers. Renaming one is a schema change, not a refactor. The list below is v0's; it is not closed, and a consumer must treat an unrecognised code as a gap it does not understand rather than as no gap.

detail.$comment: Human-readable and stable enough to assert on. A test rejects any detail under 60 characters, because a placeholder reason is how a declaration becomes paperwork.

limitation_scope.title: How wide the limitation reaches
limitation_scope.$comment: Adjacently tagged, matching GeometryPresence's shape. Ordered Profile < Document < Page in the canonical sort, so a reader meets 'this engine can never' before 'this one page could not'.

oneOf.description: True of every run under this profile, whatever the document. ALWAYS declared — including on artifacts for documents where it caused no visible harm. `multi-column-reading-order` is profile-scoped for exactly this reason: a single-column document still tells its reader that this engine would have got a two-column one wrong.

True of this document under this profile. Declared only when it applies — `font-widths-absent`, `resource-limit-pages`. `form-xobjects-not-descended` is the sharpest illustration of why the two scopes are not interchangeable: it sits beside the profile-scoped `form-xobject-text-not-descended`, which rides on every artifact and states only that this engine never descends. The document-scoped one says it happened here, and how often.
